title: Sprint Review Walk
brief: You are visiting the Meridian Digital product team on the day of a sprint review for release {{rel}} of a customer billing service. The head of delivery wants an internal audit view across intake, design, build, test, and support before the certification audit. You have 12 visit points. Cover the whole delivery chain.

actions.label: Sticky notes on the team wall
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Design review record for the invoice module
Coding standard linked from the repository
Peer review records for merged changes
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Support analyst: how customer data is handled for a fault
Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: How the team knows the quality objectives
Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Backlog items for release {{rel}}: 4 of 15 stories have no acceptance criteria, including story BIL-212 for tax rounding.
evidence.whyItMatters: Requirements must be defined well enough to design and test against. A story without acceptance criteria cannot be verified.
evidence.missedExplanation: Open several backlog items and check for testable criteria.

evidence.text: Design review record DR-31 for the invoice module lists 2 open actions marked "to do"; the module is already in build.
evidence.whyItMatters: Design reviews and verification should be completed, and actions resolved, before the design is released for build, or the risk accepted by an authorized person.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the status of actions in review records.

evidence.text: The repository links to coding standard version 2.1; the document system shows version 3.0 approved 5 months ago.
evidence.whyItMatters: People must work to the current approved version of a procedure.
evidence.missedExplanation: Follow links from tools to the document system and compare versions.

evidence.text: Test environment record TE-7 shows the database version is 2 minor versions behind production, and no comparison has been made since month 3.
evidence.whyItMatters: Test results only verify the release if the test environment represents production well enough. An unverified environment is an unreliable measuring resource.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask how the team knows the test environment matches production.

evidence.text: Support analyst: "For hard faults we export the customer's records to a spreadsheet on a laptop to look at them." No authorization record exists for export E-44 made last week.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer data is customer property. It must be protected and used only as authorized.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask how customer data is handled during support, not only in production.

evidence.text: Ticket queue report: 23 tickets are older than the 10-day target; the report is produced weekly but no one is named to review it.
evidence.whyItMatters: Monitoring data is collected but not evaluated. An owner and review would improve the response.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask who acts on each report.

evidence.text: Team lead: "Our objectives are escaped defects per release and ticket age. They are on the team page." The page shows both, updated this sprint.
evidence.whyItMatters: Staff know the objectives and their contribution.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Awareness of objectives is shown. Conforming.

evidence.text: Competence matrix: all 9 on-call staff have completed incident handling training within the last year.
evidence.whyItMatters: Competence for the role is defined and recorded.

evidence.text: Peer review records: each of the 37 merged changes this sprint shows an approving reviewer other than the author.
evidence.whyItMatters: Changes are verified before merge as planned.

evidence.text: Test summary for release {{rel}} is drafted with pass, fail, and open defect counts; sign-off is planned for tomorrow.
evidence.whyItMatters: Release verification is in progress as planned.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The summary is not signed yet because release is tomorrow. That is correct.

evidence.text: The team wall has sticky notes with ideas and reminders. None sets a requirement.
evidence.whyItMatters: Informal planning aids do not need document control.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Sticky notes for team planning are not controlled documents.

evidence.text: Chat channel names are informal, such as "billing-chat".
evidence.whyItMatters: Naming of chat channels is not a quality requirement.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Informal names do not affect conformity.

decisions.prompt: Which issue should the head of delivery act on before release {{rel}} goes out?
options: The unverified test environment and the stories without acceptance criteria, because they decide whether the release has been verified
None; the audit is next month
decisions.rationale: Issues that affect whether this release is properly verified come first. The others belong in the audit report.

containment: Before sign-off, compare the test environment with production and re-run affected tests
Stop exports of customer data until authorized handling is defined
correction: Add acceptance criteria to the 4 stories and update the repository link to coding standard 3.0
cause: Release readiness relies on individual judgment; there is no checklist covering requirements, environment, and data handling
corrective: Add a definition of ready and a release checklist that includes environment parity and data handling
effectiveness: Sample stories and environment records in the next three releases

debriefText.found: You covered the whole chain from intake to support.
debriefText.missed: In software, the test environment is a measuring resource. Ask how it is verified.
debriefText.falseFinding: Informal team tools do not need document control.
